requirements.requirement: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching
requirements.evidence: Configurator enforces SPIKE_CLASH at drawer:0#0,0#cut corner junction -1,0|-1,1|0,0 – placing spike there after drawer is refused (and vice versa). Built closest verifiable alternative: drawer on half-s cell at 0,0,0 (its cut face) and spike at adjacent junction -1,1|0,0|0,1 touching the same cell (0,0) – physically touching the drawer cell, one corner away, meshClash clear.

finish.summary: Requested identical-corner drawer+spike is blocked by configurator rule SPIKE_CLASH (spike stands where drawer fills). Built nearest allowed touching arrangement: half-s base at 0,0 with north-facing drawer, plus three full bases to create hexagonal cluster, spike at junction -1,1|0,0|0,1 which shares the drawer cell and touches it. Mesh verified clear, faces capped and joints locked.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

result.note: A drawer sits on the cut face of a half base: place a half base (variant half-n, half-s, half-e or half-w) first. No place on the build takes this part right now. A spike stands where three bases meet at a corner: place three bases around one junction first. No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.
